1. THE TWO EXACT MACRO BRANCHES AND STATEMENT

Use the ordinary square zero-boundary model and fixed SAME-diagonal
affine interpolant Phi_n from the immutable terminal theorem:
 SQUARE_GAUSSIAN_TERMINAL_THEOREM.txt, SHA256
 1b813c5eb684f8fecc9994d8ee6bba464bfaa1691e73d9addf0b2887e43bcd05.
In particular h is globally extended by zero on E_n=Z^2 minus V_n;
every original nearest-neighbor increment has magnitude <=1; all scaled
polygon supports lie in one fixed bounded box; outside triangles have
only zero vertices. No 1/n height factor is present. Let eta_{n,u} be
the FULL-plane nodal hats of the fixed triangulation for EVERY u in Z^2,
including fixed zero vertices. They are nonnegative, sum to one, have
integral n^-2, and support radius <=sqrt(2)/n about u/n.

The FULL supplied macro theorem has the following scope. For every fixed
c0,C0>0 and every R>=1, every deterministic finite real weight family q
on the ambient lattice satisfying
 sum|q_u|<=C0, max|q_u|<=C0 R^-2,
 supp(q) contained in a box of diameter<=C0 R,
has E exp(a|sum q_u h_u|)<=M with a>0,M<infinity uniform over volume,
R and q, provided EITHER
 (Z) sum_u q_u=0 EXACTLY,
 OR
 (P) a connected zero-pin set K of diameter>=c0 R lies with supp(q)
     in a box of diameter<=C0 R.
The weights may include fixed vertices; their zero HEIGHT VALUES may
be dropped in the statistic, but their WEIGHTS must be retained when
checking (Z). The frozen macro target explicitly permits these ambient
weights. Only zero data are used here.

Its exact statement/proof pins are target af8e03461c60e3e6aa86734d85f0e2622f03fa2f8dfb9eddd8911497b941eabd
and zero-data proof03ce1c7b494e6f0b7fb93e6f590c11556126978bb9c948210aece9b715a4fcaa.
The anchored branch alone is insufficient for the local argument.

THEOREM I (tightness, without a Gaussian premise).
For every r>0 there is C_r<infinity, independent of n, with
       sup_n E||Phi_n||_{H^{-r}(T)}^2<=C_r,                (1.1)
where T is one fixed torus containing all supports. Thus Phi_n is tight
in H^{-s}(T) for EVERY s>0, by choosing 0<r<s. Constants may depend
on r, the fixed torus/mesh, the kernel and macro constants. They are
not asserted uniform as r decreases to zero.
